_rules: A session's identity is GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL looked up HERE; a name with no row cannot write to the ledger (ledger-db.sh refuses with exit 3).
Add a row when an agent is onboarded; never delete one — set status to retired with the date, so the ledger's claimed_by stays attributable forever.

The onboarding script that writes rows here and prints the launch line arrives with feat_harness_identity_comes_from_the_session_via_a_roster_and_session_entries_are_ledger_rows; until then edit this file by hand in a PR.
role is one of: product-owner, developer, head-of-testing, process-improvement (docs/roles/).

agents.name: Example
agents.evidence: a template row showing the shape; retired so it can never claim — replace it with your first real agent

_machines_note: MACHINES are a third population, in the same file for the same reason as humans: an unattended unit is not an agent (no role prompt, no claims, never routed to) but must prove a SESSION identity, because the ledger refuses every write whose name came from a directory. A machine row's email goes on its unit as Environment=GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL; its database role is created by a migration that grants exactly what the unit needs (read-only = ledger_console), never by the agent sync. Records, not a rota: a listing helper never returns one.
_assistants_note: ASSISTANTS are people's helpers that act under a person's authority (an assistant's row names whose). Records, not a rota: never routed to, never listed as active agents.
